option_description: Controls whether presigned URLs or delegated storage access tokens can be redeemed by clients located outside the defined storage trust zone, specifically whether the object storage endpoint resolves and serves presigned URL requests from external or less-trusted network zones without requiring traversal of zone ingress controls.
security_impact: The Rego rule 'object_storage_presigned_url_bypass_of_boundary_controls' triggers when both presigned_url_generation_enabled and presigned_url_accessible_from_external_zone are true. This combination means storage objects become accessible to any external party who possesses a valid URL, completely bypassing zone boundary network controls. This directly enables T1530 (Data from Cloud Storage) and T1528 (Steal Application Access Token) attacks where intercepted URLs grant full object access from outside the security perimeter.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Generate a test presigned URL for a non-sensitive object in the storage bucket and attempt to redeem it from a host outside the storage trust zone (e.g., from a public internet machine or a different VPC without peering). Confirm whether the request succeeds or is blocked.
how_to_obtain.command: PRESIGNED=$(aws s3 presign s3://<bucket>/<test-object> --expires-in 300) && curl -v -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "$PRESIGNED"
how_to_obtain.expected_output: HTTP 200 from an external host confirms presigned URLs are accessible from outside the zone; HTTP 403 with VPC endpoint policy denial or network block confirms zone restriction is enforced.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the S3 VPC endpoint policy to determine whether it restricts presigned URL redemption to requests originating from within the storage VPC, or whether the bucket is also publicly accessible via the global S3 endpoint.
how_to_obtain.command: aws ec2 describe-vpc-endpoints --filters Name=vpc-id,Values=<storage-vpc-id> Name=service-name,Values=com.amazonaws.<region>.s3 --query 'VpcEndpoints[*].{PolicyDocument:PolicyDocument,State:State}' --output json | jq '.[].PolicyDocument | fromjson'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: VPC endpoint policy with Condition restricting aws:sourceVpc to the storage VPC and no public bucket access block override indicates external zone access is prevented; permissive 'Allow *' policy confirms external accessibility.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check S3 bucket public access block settings and bucket ACL to determine whether the bucket endpoint is reachable from the public internet, which would make presigned URLs accessible from any external zone.
how_to_obtain.command: aws s3api get-public-access-block --bucket <storage-bucket-name> && aws s3api get-bucket-acl --bucket <storage-bucket-name> | jq '.Grants[] | select(.Grantee.URI | test("AllUsers|AuthenticatedUsers"))'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: All four PublicAccessBlock settings set to true and no AllUsers/AuthenticatedUsers ACL grants indicates the bucket endpoint is not publicly reachable; any false setting or public grant confirms external zone accessibility.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review Terraform IaC for the storage bucket resource and VPC endpoint module to confirm whether vpc_endpoint_policy resources restrict presigned URL redemption to internal zone source VPCs.
how_to_obtain.command: grep -A20 'aws_vpc_endpoint_policy\|aws_s3_bucket_policy' <iac-repo-path>/storage.tf | grep -E '(aws:sourceVpc|aws:sourceVpce|Condition)'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Condition blocks containing aws:sourceVpc or aws:sourceVpce conditions scoped to the storage VPC ID confirm zone restriction on presigned URL redemption; absence of these conditions confirms external accessibility.

option_description: Controls the maximum permitted lifetime in seconds for presigned URLs or delegated storage access tokens generated by the object storage service. This integer value caps how long a generated URL remains valid for object access, with shorter durations limiting the exposure window if a URL is intercepted, logged, cached, or shared beyond its intended recipient.
security_impact: The Rego rule 'object_storage_presigned_url_bypass_of_boundary_controls' includes a condition checking presigned_url_max_validity_seconds > 86400 (24 hours) alongside external zone accessibility. Extended validity periods significantly increase the risk window for T1550.001 (Application Access Token) abuse — a URL valid for 7 days (604800 seconds) found in a log file, browser history, or CDN cache provides attackers a multi-day exploitation window for T1530 (Data from Cloud Storage) without any credential or boundary re-traversal requirement.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Scan application code and CI/CD scripts for presigned URL generation calls and extract the expiry/TTL parameter values to determine the maximum duration in use.
how_to_obtain.command: grep -rE '(ExpiresIn|expires_in|expiry|Expiry|ttl|TTL|validity).*[0-9]+' <application-repo-path>/ --include='*.py' --include='*.js' --include='*.go' --include='*.java' | grep -iE '(presign|signed_url|sas|token)' | sort -t= -k2 -rn | head -20
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Lines showing expiry values; the maximum integer value found across all occurrences is the effective max validity. Values > 86400 indicate high-risk configuration.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query CloudTrail S3 data events to extract presigned URL expiration durations from GetObject requests using query-string authentication by examining the X-Amz-Expires query parameter in the request URLs.
how_to_obtain.command: aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventName,AttributeValue=GetObject --start-time $(date -d '24 hours ago' --iso-8601=seconds) --output json | jq '.Events[].CloudTrailEvent | fromjson | select(.requestParameters.url | test("X-Amz-Expires")) | .requestParameters.url | capture("X-Amz-Expires=(?P<expiry>[0-9]+)") | .expiry | tonumber' | sort -rn | head -5
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Numeric expiry values in seconds sorted descending; the highest value represents the maximum presigned URL validity observed. Values above 3600 warrant review; above 86400 indicate high risk.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review AWS Service Control Policies (SCPs) or GCP Organization Policies for constraints that cap presigned URL expiry durations at an organizational level.
how_to_obtain.command: aws organizations list-policies --filter SERVICE_CONTROL_POLICY --output json | jq -r '.Policies[].Id' | xargs -I{} aws organizations describe-policy --policy-id {} --output json | jq '.Policy.Content | fromjson | .Statement[] | select(.Condition | tostring | test("s3:signatureAge|presigned"))'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: SCP statements with Condition on s3:signatureAge confirming a maximum age enforcement; absence of such conditions means no organizational cap is enforced and application-level values are authoritative.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Use the AWS Config advanced query to find all S3 bucket configurations and cross-reference with Lambda or application-tier environment variables that set presigned URL expiry defaults.
how_to_obtain.command: aws lambda list-functions --query 'Functions[*].FunctionName' --output text | tr '\t' '\n' | xargs -I{} aws lambda get-function-configuration --function-name {} --query 'Environment.Variables' --output json 2>/dev/null | jq 'to_entries[] | select(.key | test("PRESIGNED|EXPIRY|URL_TTL|SIGNED_URL")) | {key:.key, value:.value}'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Environment variable keys and values showing configured expiry durations; values expressed in seconds above 3600 indicate extended validity; above 86400 confirms the Rego high-risk threshold is breached.

option_description: Records the shortest (most permissive) prefix length found among all ingress firewall, security group, or ACL rules protecting storage zone endpoints. A prefix length of 0 means 0.0.0.0/0 (all traffic allowed); 32 means a single host. Smaller values indicate broader, less restrictive source address ranges permitted inbound to database and object storage services.
security_impact: The Rego rule boundary_rule_permitting_broad_source_cidr_ranges triggers an exposure when ingress_cidr_prefix_length is less than or equal to 16 and service_tag_or_specific_ip_used is false. A /16 or shorter prefix allows up to 65,536 hosts to reach storage endpoints, dramatically expanding the attack surface for techniques like T1595.001 (Scanning IP Blocks) and T1599 (Network Boundary Bridging). Identifying the minimum prefix length surfaces the single most permissive rule that could be exploited.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On AWS, list all security group ingress rules associated with RDS and S3 VPC endpoints, then identify the rule with the shortest prefix length using the AWS CLI.
how_to_obtain.command: aws ec2 describe-security-groups --filters Name=tag:Zone,Values=storage --query 'SecurityGroups[*].IpPermissions[*].IpRanges[*].CidrIp' --output text | awk -F'/' '{print $2}' | sort -n | head -1
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A single integer (e.g., 10) representing the shortest prefix length found. A value of 0 means a 0.0.0.0/0 rule exists.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On Azure, inspect Network Security Group inbound rules for storage-zone NSGs and extract the minimum destination address prefix length.
how_to_obtain.command: az network nsg list --query '[?tags.Zone==`storage`].securityRules[?direction==`Inbound`].sourceAddressPrefix' -o tsv | grep -oP '/\K[0-9]+' | sort -n | head -1
how_to_obtain.expected_output: An integer representing the shortest prefix length among all inbound rules (e.g., 8 for a /8 rule).

how_to_obtain.instruction: In the AWS Console, navigate to VPC > Security Groups, filter by the storage zone tag, open each group, select the Inbound Rules tab, and review the Source column for the broadest CIDR entry. Record the prefix length (number after the slash).
how_to_obtain.navigation: AWS Console > VPC > Security Groups > [storage zone group] > Inbound Rules > Source column
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Identification of the most permissive inbound CIDR rule, e.g., 10.0.0.0/8 yields prefix length 8.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Use the GCP REST API to list firewall rules targeting storage instance tags and extract the minimum prefix length from sourceRanges.
how_to_obtain.command: curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)' 'https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/global/firewalls' | jq '[.items[] | select(.targetTags[] == "storage-zone") | .sourceRanges[] | split("/")[1] | tonumber] | min'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A JSON integer representing the minimum prefix length among all matching firewall ingress rules.

option_description: Records the shortest (most permissive) prefix length found among all outbound firewall, security group, or ACL rules on the storage zone boundary. A smaller value indicates a broader destination address range is permitted for outbound connections from storage components, increasing the risk of unauthorized data exfiltration to wide address spaces.
security_impact: The Rego rule boundary_rule_permitting_broad_source_cidr_ranges also fires on egress_cidr_prefix_length when it is less than or equal to 16 and service_tag_or_specific_ip_used is false. Overly broad egress destinations enable data exfiltration techniques T1567.002 (Exfiltration to Cloud Storage) and T1048 (Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol), and support C2 beacon paths if a storage component is compromised. The minimum egress prefix length reveals the single most permissive outbound path.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On AWS, query security group outbound rules for storage-zone groups and identify the shortest destination CIDR prefix.
how_to_obtain.command: aws ec2 describe-security-groups --filters Name=tag:Zone,Values=storage --query 'SecurityGroups[*].IpPermissionsEgress[*].IpRanges[*].CidrIp' --output text | awk -F'/' '{print $2}' | sort -n | head -1
how_to_obtain.expected_output: An integer such as 0 (for 0.0.0.0/0) or 24. A value of 0 indicates fully unrestricted egress.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On Linux-based firewall hosts, inspect iptables or nftables OUTPUT chain rules protecting storage zone interfaces and extract the minimum destination prefix.
how_to_obtain.command: iptables -L OUTPUT -n --line-numbers | grep -oP '\d+\.\d+\.\d+\.\d+/\K\d+' | sort -n | head -1
how_to_obtain.expected_output: An integer prefix length, e.g., 16. If no output is returned, all egress may be permitted with 0.0.0.0/0 or no rules.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In the Azure Portal, open the Network Security Group associated with the storage subnet, select Outbound Security Rules, sort by Destination, and record the prefix length of the broadest destination CIDR entry.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Azure Portal > Network Security Groups > [storage NSG] > Outbound Security Rules > Destination column
how_to_obtain.expected_output: The most permissive outbound CIDR rule visible, e.g., 0.0.0.0/0 or 10.0.0.0/8.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Use the AWS SDK to enumerate egress rules and compute the minimum prefix length programmatically.
how_to_obtain.command: python3 -c "import boto3,ipaddress; ec2=boto3.client('ec2'); sgs=ec2.describe_security_groups(Filters=[{'Name':'tag:Zone','Values':['storage']}])['SecurityGroups']; prefixes=[int(r['CidrIp'].split('/')[1]) for sg in sgs for p in sg['IpPermissionsEgress'] for r in p.get('IpRanges',[])] ; print(min(prefixes) if prefixes else 'no rules')"
how_to_obtain.expected_output: An integer such as 0 or 24 indicating the minimum egress prefix length across all storage-zone security groups.

option_description: Indicates whether all permissive ingress and egress rules on the storage zone boundary reference named service tags (e.g., AWS prefix lists, Azure service tags) or specific /32 host IP addresses rather than broad CIDR blocks. Must be true only when every rule uses this precise form of source or destination specification.
security_impact: The Rego rule boundary_rule_permitting_broad_source_cidr_ranges uses this as a mitigating control: if service_tag_or_specific_ip_used is true, the broad-CIDR exposure does not fire even when ingress_cidr_prefix_length or egress_cidr_prefix_length is 16 or smaller. Service tags and specific IPs constrain access to well-known managed services rather than entire network blocks, preventing T1595.001 (Scanning IP Blocks) and T1599 (Network Boundary Bridging). If any permissive rule uses a generic CIDR, this attribute must be false.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On AWS, check whether storage-zone security group rules use managed prefix lists (service tags) rather than raw CIDRs by inspecting the PrefixListIds field.
how_to_obtain.command: aws ec2 describe-security-groups --filters Name=tag:Zone,Values=storage --query 'SecurityGroups[*].IpPermissions[*].PrefixListIds' --output json | python3 -c "import sys,json; data=json.load(sys.stdin); print('true' if all(len(pl)>0 for sg in data for rule in sg for pl in [rule] if rule) else 'check each rule')"
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Output indicating whether prefix list IDs are present in all permissive rules. Presence of empty IpRanges arrays alongside populated PrefixListIds suggests service tags are in use.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On Azure, verify that NSG rules for the storage subnet use Azure Service Tags in the sourceAddressPrefix field rather than raw CIDRs.
how_to_obtain.command: az network nsg list --query '[?tags.Zone==`storage`].securityRules[].{src:sourceAddressPrefix,dst:destinationAddressPrefix}' -o json | python3 -c "import sys,json,ipaddress; rules=json.load(sys.stdin); tag_or_host=all(not r['src'].replace('/','').replace('.','').isdigit() or ipaddress.ip_network(r['src'],strict=False).prefixlen==32 for r in rules if r['src'] not in ['*','Internet','Any']); print(tag_or_host)"
how_to_obtain.expected_output: True if all rules reference service tags or /32 hosts; False if any rule uses a broad CIDR.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In the AWS Console, navigate to VPC > Security Groups > [storage zone group] > Inbound/Outbound Rules and inspect the Source/Destination column. Look for entries that show a prefix list name (pl-xxxxxxxx) or a /32 address. Any raw CIDR shorter than /32 without a prefix list reference means this attribute is false.
how_to_obtain.navigation: AWS Console > VPC > Security Groups > [storage zone group] > Inbound Rules / Outbound Rules > Source or Destination column
how_to_obtain.expected_output: All entries show prefix list names or /32 IPs. If any entry shows e.g. 10.0.0.0/8, the attribute value is false.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For Terraform-managed infrastructure, inspect the security group resource blocks and verify that all cidr_blocks arguments use /32 addresses or that the rule references aws_ec2_managed_prefix_list resources instead of raw CIDRs.
how_to_obtain.command: grep -rE 'cidr_blocks|prefix_list_ids' infrastructure/security_groups.tf | grep -v '/32'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No output means all rules use /32 CIDRs or prefix lists. Any output reveals broad CIDR rules and indicates the attribute should be false.

option_description: Indicates whether the storage zone boundary gateway, service mesh, or load balancer requires both the client and the server to present valid X.509 certificates for every service-to-service connection crossing the boundary. True means bidirectional certificate verification is mandatory for all connections; false means only server-side TLS or no TLS is enforced.
security_impact: The Rego rule lack_of_mutual_authentication_at_zone_boundary fires when mutual_tls_enforced is false (the not input.mutual_tls_enforced condition). Without mTLS, spoofed service-to-service connections can traverse the boundary using techniques T1649 (Steal or Forge Authentication Certificates), T1199 (Trusted Relationship abuse), and T1572 (Protocol Tunneling). Enforcing mTLS ensures that even if network-level controls are bypassed, impersonated services cannot authenticate successfully.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For Istio service mesh, check the PeerAuthentication policy in the storage zone namespace to confirm mTLS mode is STRICT.
how_to_obtain.command: kubectl get peerauthentication -n storage-zone -o jsonpath='{.items[*].spec.mtls.mode}'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: STRICT indicates mutual TLS is enforced. PERMISSIVE or empty means mTLS is not fully enforced and the attribute is false.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For an nginx boundary proxy, inspect the SSL configuration for ssl_verify_client directives indicating client certificate requirements.
how_to_obtain.command: grep -rE 'ssl_verify_client|ssl_client_certificate' /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/ /etc/nginx/conf.d/
how_to_obtain.expected_output: ssl_verify_client on; indicates mTLS is enforced. ssl_verify_client optional or its absence means the attribute is false.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For AWS API Gateway or NLB with mutual TLS, check whether trustStoreUri is configured on the domain name or listener, indicating client certificate validation is active.
how_to_obtain.command: aws apigatewayv2 get-domain-names --query 'Items[?DomainNameConfigurations[?MutualTlsAuthentication.TruststoreUri!=null]].DomainName' --output text
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Domain names listed indicate mTLS is configured. Empty output means no mTLS trust store is configured and the attribute is false.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For Envoy proxy at the zone boundary, inspect the DownstreamTlsContext in the listener configuration for require_client_certificate set to true.
how_to_obtain.command: cat /etc/envoy/envoy.yaml | python3 -c "import sys,yaml; cfg=yaml.safe_load(sys.stdin); listeners=cfg.get('static_resources',{}).get('listeners',[]); [print(l) for l in listeners if 'require_client_certificate' in str(l)]"
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Output containing require_client_certificate: true confirms mTLS enforcement. Absence or false value means the attribute is false.

option_description: Describes the specific mode of client certificate validation enforced at the storage zone boundary ingress component. 'required' means every connecting client must present a valid, trusted certificate or the connection is rejected. 'optional' means certificates are accepted and inspected if provided but the connection proceeds without one. 'none' means no client certificate is requested or validated.
security_impact: The Rego rule lack_of_mutual_authentication_at_zone_boundary fires when client_certificate_validation_mode is 'optional' or 'none'. Optional mode is particularly dangerous because it creates a false sense of security: certificates may be logged but connections without certificates still succeed, allowing unauthenticated service impersonation via T1199 and T1649. Only 'required' mode provides the cryptographic proof of client identity needed to prevent spoofed cross-zone connections.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the nginx TLS configuration for the storage zone ingress to determine the ssl_verify_client setting value.
how_to_obtain.command: grep -h 'ssl_verify_client' /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/* /etc/nginx/conf.d/* 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $2}' | tr -d ';'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: on maps to required; optional maps to optional; off or absent maps to none.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For Istio, extract the mTLS mode from PeerAuthentication resources in the storage zone namespace to determine validation strictness.
how_to_obtain.command: kubectl get peerauthentication -n storage-zone -o json | jq -r '.items[].spec.mtls.mode // "none"'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: STRICT maps to required; PERMISSIVE maps to optional; DISABLE or absence maps to none.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For HAProxy acting as the boundary proxy, check the verify parameter in the bind directive to determine client certificate validation mode.
how_to_obtain.command: grep -E 'bind.*ssl' /etc/haproxy/haproxy.cfg | grep -oE 'verify (required|optional|none)'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: verify required confirms the attribute is required; verify optional maps to optional; absence of verify or verify none maps to none.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In the AWS ALB Console, navigate to Load Balancers > [storage zone ALB] > Listeners > [HTTPS listener] > Edit and check the Mutual Authentication (mTLS) section for the mode setting.
how_to_obtain.navigation: AWS Console > EC2 > Load Balancers > [ALB] > Listeners > [HTTPS:443] > Edit Listener > Mutual Authentication
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Passthrough with certificate validation set to Verify with Trust Store maps to required. Passthrough without verification or no mTLS setting maps to optional or none.

option_description: Indicates whether traffic originating from internal or trusted network zones is permitted to reach storage zone services without presenting authentication credentials at the boundary. When true, source IP address or subnet membership is used as implicit trust, allowing service-to-service calls without certificate or token-based authentication.
security_impact: The Rego rule lack_of_mutual_authentication_at_zone_boundary fires when internal_zone_traffic_authentication_bypass is true. This configuration directly enables lateral movement after initial compromise: an attacker who gains a foothold in any internal zone can reach storage endpoints without further credential challenge. This supports T1199 (Trusted Relationship) and T1572 (Protocol Tunneling) exploitation patterns. IP-based trust is insufficient because internal IPs can be spoofed or compromised hosts can initiate connections from trusted subnets.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For Istio, check AuthorizationPolicy resources in the storage zone namespace for rules that allow traffic based solely on source namespace or IP without requiring a valid principal (mTLS identity).
how_to_obtain.command: kubectl get authorizationpolicy -n storage-zone -o json | jq '.items[] | select(.spec.rules[].from[].source | has("ipBlocks") and (has("principals") | not)) | .metadata.name'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Policy names returned indicate authentication bypass rules exist and the attribute is true. Empty output suggests all rules require authenticated principals.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review firewall or security group rules to identify any rules that allow inbound access from internal RFC1918 ranges to storage ports without a corresponding authentication requirement in an application-layer policy.
how_to_obtain.command: aws ec2 describe-security-groups --filters Name=tag:Zone,Values=storage --query 'SecurityGroups[*].IpPermissions[?contains(IpRanges[*].CidrIp, `10.0.0.0/8`) || contains(IpRanges[*].CidrIp, `172.16.0.0/12`) || contains(IpRanges[*].CidrIp, `192.168.0.0/16`)]' --output json
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Any non-empty result shows RFC1918 source ranges allowed at the network layer. Cross-reference with application authentication policy to determine if those connections also bypass authentication.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Interview the platform or network security team to determine whether any documented exception exists that permits internal zone traffic to bypass token or certificate authentication. Review the security architecture decision records (ADRs) for storage zone access policies.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Documentation of a formal exemption for internal traffic confirms bypass is in place (true). No documented exception and enforcement of credentials for all callers confirms the attribute is false.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For Kong API Gateway at the storage boundary, inspect plugin configurations to check whether the jwt or mtls-auth plugin is disabled or has an allow_list that exempts internal CIDR ranges.
how_to_obtain.command: kubectl get kongplugin -n storage-zone -o json | jq '.items[] | select(.plugin == "jwt" or .plugin == "mtls-auth") | {name: .metadata.name, config: .config}'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: If no jwt or mtls-auth plugin is found, or if skip_consumer_groups or exempted IP ranges are configured, the attribute is likely true.

option_description: Indicates whether all storage zone components (database instances, object storage proxies, sidecar containers) are configured to use exclusively an internal, authoritative DNS resolver rather than public resolvers such as 8.8.8.8 or 1.1.1.1. When true, no storage component can initiate a DNS query to an external resolver.
security_impact: The Rego rule dns_resolution_not_constrained_within_storage_zone fires when dns_resolver_restricted_to_internal is false (the not input.dns_resolver_restricted_to_internal condition appears in all three branches). Unrestricted DNS resolver configuration enables DNS-based data exfiltration (T1071.004 DNS C2), fast flux DNS evasion (T1568.001), and DNS server hijacking (T1584.002). An attacker with code execution in the storage zone can encode data in DNS query names to an external resolver, bypassing egress IP filters entirely.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On Linux-based storage zone hosts or containers, inspect the resolv.conf file to confirm that only internal resolver IPs are listed in the nameserver directives.
how_to_obtain.command: cat /etc/resolv.conf | grep nameserver
how_to_obtain.expected_output: All nameserver lines should reference internal IP addresses (e.g., 10.0.0.2). Any public IP such as 8.8.8.8, 1.1.1.1, or 9.9.9.9 means the attribute is false.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For Kubernetes deployments in the storage namespace, inspect CoreDNS ConfigMap and pod DNS configuration to verify no external forwarders are configured.
how_to_obtain.command: kubectl get configmap coredns -n kube-system -o jsonpath='{.data.Corefile}' | grep -E 'forward|nameserver'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: forward . /etc/resolv.conf pointing to an internal resolver is acceptable. forward . 8.8.8.8 or similar external addresses means the attribute is false.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For AWS RDS or EC2 storage instances, verify that the DHCP Options Set associated with the VPC specifies only internal Route 53 Resolver or custom resolver IPs.
how_to_obtain.command: aws ec2 describe-dhcp-options --dhcp-options-ids $(aws ec2 describe-vpcs --filters Name=tag:Zone,Values=storage --query 'Vpcs[0].DhcpOptionsId' --output text) --query 'DhcpOptions[0].DhcpConfigurations[?Key==`domain-name-servers`].Values[*].Value' --output text
how_to_obtain.expected_output: AmazonProvidedDNS or a private IP (e.g., 10.0.0.2) is acceptable for internal resolution. Any public DNS IP confirms the attribute is false.

how_to_obtain.instruction: From within a storage zone host or container, attempt a DNS resolution to an external domain using a known public resolver to verify whether outbound DNS to external resolvers is possible.
how_to_obtain.command: dig @8.8.8.8 example.com +timeout=3 +tries=1; echo "Exit code: $?"
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A timeout or connection refused response (exit code 9) confirms external DNS is blocked and the configuration is correctly restricted. A successful resolution means the attribute is false.

option_description: Indicates whether outbound UDP and TCP traffic on port 53 from storage zone components is explicitly blocked at the network boundary for all destinations except a designated internal resolver endpoint. This is a network-layer enforcement complementary to host-based DNS resolver configuration, ensuring that even if a storage component's resolv.conf is modified, DNS queries to external resolvers cannot egress the zone.
security_impact: The Rego rule dns_resolution_not_constrained_within_storage_zone fires when egress_dns_port_restricted is false (the not input.egress_dns_port_restricted condition appears in two of the three branches). Network-level port 53 restriction is a defense-in-depth control: even if dns_resolver_restricted_to_internal is true at the host level, an attacker with local code execution could modify resolver configuration or use raw sockets. Blocking port 53 at the boundary prevents T1071.004 (DNS C2), T1568.001 (Fast Flux DNS), and T1584.002 (DNS Server hijacking) by eliminating the network path entirely.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On AWS, check security group outbound rules for storage-zone groups to confirm port 53 egress is denied to all except the internal resolver IP.
how_to_obtain.command: aws ec2 describe-security-groups --filters Name=tag:Zone,Values=storage --query 'SecurityGroups[*].IpPermissionsEgress[?contains(FromPort,`53`) || contains(ToPort,`53`)]' --output json
how_to_obtain.expected_output: An empty array or rules listing only the internal resolver CIDR (e.g., 10.0.0.2/32) on port 53 confirms restriction. Rules permitting 0.0.0.0/0 on port 53 mean the attribute is false.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On Linux hosts at the storage zone perimeter, inspect iptables OUTPUT rules to verify that UDP and TCP port 53 egress is restricted.
how_to_obtain.command: iptables -L OUTPUT -n | grep -E '(dpt:53|REJECT|DROP)' | grep 53
how_to_obtain.expected_output: DROP or REJECT rules for dpt:53 to destinations other than the internal resolver confirm restriction. Absence of such rules or a blanket ACCEPT means the attribute is false.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For Azure, verify that the storage subnet Network Security Group has an outbound deny rule for port 53 to Internet and all non-resolver destinations.
how_to_obtain.command: az network nsg list --query '[?tags.Zone==`storage`].securityRules[?direction==`Outbound` && destinationPortRange==`53`].{name:name,access:access,dest:destinationAddressPrefix}' -o table
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Rows showing Deny access for port 53 to * or Internet, combined with an Allow rule for the internal resolver IP only, confirm restriction. Missing deny rules or a blanket allow means the attribute is false.

how_to_obtain.instruction: From within a storage zone component, attempt a DNS query directly to an external public resolver on port 53 to verify whether the network boundary blocks it.
how_to_obtain.command: nc -u -z -w 3 8.8.8.8 53; echo "UDP exit: $?"; nc -z -w 3 8.8.8.8 53; echo "TCP exit: $?"
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Non-zero exit codes for both UDP and TCP connections to 8.8.8.8:53 confirm egress port 53 is restricted (attribute is true). Exit code 0 on either test means the connection succeeded and the attribute is false.
